data.narrative:
Nuro, a Series G autonomous delivery drone company founded by Dave Ferguson and Jiajun Zhu, is evaluated against a peer set of four private and public-equivalent entities in the Drones & Autonomous sector. The comparable universe includes Zipline ($7.6B Series G), Joby Aviation ($6.9B public), Archer Aviation ($3.3B public), and Elroy Air, spanning similar technology and commercialization stages.

Two valuation methods anchor this analysis. The stage-progression approach applies a 1.25x step-up multiplier to Nuro's last post-money valuation of $6.0B, yielding $7.5B. The peer-median method derives a $6.9B implied value from three directly comparable companies with valuations ranging $3.3B to $7.6B. These methods produce a triangulated range of $5.8B (low) to $8.6B (high), with a median of $7.2B. The current $6.0B valuation sits in the lower half of this range.

Key uncertainties center on the narrow peer set—only four comparables in an emerging sector—and valuation dispersion reflecting heterogeneous commercialization timelines and cash burn profiles. The $3.3B floor (Archer Aviation) and $7.6B ceiling (Zipline) suggest meaningful disagreement on unit economics and path to profitability. Against $2.2B raised to date, the median $7.2B implies capital efficiency assumptions that warrant scrutiny against revenue and near-term path to positive unit economics.
